main_text.p: liæ & epilepsiæ causis, & differentijs tra-ctat:Deinde commentario sexto,in librum sextum Epidimiorum Hippocratis, ubi epilepsiæ causam esse crassum humorem & frigidum in cerebri ventriculis affluxũ co-prehendentem nervorum originem,atque in primis initium spinalis medullę apertis-simè exprimit. Ubi etiamnum addit eum, qui prius quartana febre correptus fuerit, epilepsia non corripi, & febres diuturnio-res,& præ omnibus quartanas,quę longis-simæ sunt, quæq; rigore suas accefsiones sortiuntur,epilepticum humore discutere.

Oribasius,Areteus,ut & Aëtius, atq; etiam Paulus Æginęta,& Actuarius,qui post Galenum medicinam gloriosè exercuerunt, idem nobis scriptum reliquerunt:atq; ad eam epilepsiam, quæ proprio cerebri affe-ctu fit, veratrum utrunq; & colocynthida, quæ crassos humores & viscidos è capite evacuat, unà cum victus ratione,quæ attenuat, & exiccat præscripserunt. Quapropter morbus comitialis,qui proprius est cerebri affectus à crasso humore & frigido originem ducit, & consequenter a veneno intus genito non fit.

page.notes: The page begins mid-sentence ("liæ"), so the opening fragment is kept as a fragment. "affluxũ" carries a tilde that may stand for a final -m or -u; read as printed. Two lines near the end ("a veneno intus genito", "non fit.") are set indented and are treated as the continuation of the same paragraph. No catchword or signature is visible. The ligature "ct" in "tra-ctat" and "Actuarius" is printed as a ct ligature.
